how do I add my homepage to it and then add it to my domain

To add this exact single-file HTML layout into your Next.js project and deploy it to your domain, follow these steps.

Since Next.js uses React components instead of vanilla HTML script tags, the cleanest and fastest way to bring this exact file over without breaking changes is to place it inside your Next.js public folder as an HTML file, or convert it to a React component.

Method 1: The Quickest Way (Run it as your main page using HTML)
If you want to drop your exact HTML file straight into Next.js without rewriting it into React state, you can serve it directly from the public directory.

Move your HTML file:
Take your HTML file, rename it to index.html, and place it directly into the public/ folder of your project (cool-real-estate-tools/public/index.html).

Clear the default Next.js page:
Delete or empty out the code inside src/app/page.tsx so it doesn't conflict. You can make it a simple redirect or return a basic container, or even better, configure Next.js to serve static exports. Alternatively, you can use a minimal redirect script inside src/app/page.tsx:

TypeScript
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
export default function Page() {
  redirect('/index.html');
}
(Note: Moving your HTML file to public/index.html allows Vercel to serve it instantly with all JavaScript and Tailwind scripts working out of the box).

Method 2: Deploying to Your Domain (Vercel)
Once your code is inside your project repository, deploy it live:

Initialize Git & Push to GitHub:
Open your terminal inside your project folder and run:

Bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit of cool real estate tools"
Create a new repository on your GitHub account, then push your code:

Bash
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/cool-real-estate-tools.git
git push -u origin main
Connect to Vercel:

Go to Vercel.com and log in.

Click Add New Project and import your cool-real-estate-tools GitHub repository.

Leave the build settings as default and click Deploy.

Attach Your Custom Domain:

Once the deployment is successful, go to your project dashboard on Vercel.

Click on the Settings tab at the top, then click Domains on the left sidebar.

Enter your custom domain name (e.g., coolrealestatetools.com) and click Add.

Vercel will provide you with standard DNS records (like an A record or CNAME). Log into where you bought your domain (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Google Domains/Squarespace, etc.), paste those DNS records into your domain manager, and your site will go live securely with free SSL!

is doing the index.html better than reformatting it for app.tsk

Yes, keeping the single-file HTML approach (by placing it in the public/ folder) is often much better and more practical for this specific project stack than rewriting it into a React component (app/page.tsx), for several reasons:

Zero-Refactoring Friction: Your HTML file relies heavily on vanilla JavaScript functions (switchView, calculateNet, submitOpenHouse) and DOM manipulation IDs (document.getElementById). Converting it to Next.js requires completely rewriting the view-switching and state management logic into React hooks, which is prone to state errors and missing tool elements.

Instant Deployment: By putting the file in public/index.html, Next.js and Vercel serve it directly as a static file, meaning all your Tailwind CDN scripts, Google Fonts, and interactive click events work immediately without build errors.

Preserved Functionality: It guarantees that none of your micro-apps, modals, or styling views get accidentally left out or broken during a JSX translation.

remote: Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported for Git operations.

fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/notxesnad/cret.git/'

This error happens because GitHub no longer allows you to use your standard account password when pushing code via the command line (https:// URLs). You need to authenticate using a Personal Access Token (PAT) instead of your password, or switch your repository connection to use SSH.

Here is how to fix it quickly:

Method 1: Use a Personal Access Token (PAT) (Easiest)
Generate a Token on GitHub:

Go to GitHub.com, click your profile picture in the top right, and go to Settings.

Scroll down the left sidebar and click Developer settings (at the very bottom).

Click Personal access tokens -> Tokens (classic) (or Fine-grained tokens).

Click Generate new token (classic).

Give it a note (e.g., "CLI Access"), check the repo scope checkbox (this grants full control of private and public repositories), and click Generate token at the bottom.

Copy the token string immediately (it looks like a long string of letters and numbers). Save it somewhere safe, as GitHub won't show it to you again.

Push your code again:

Run your git push command again.

When it asks for your Username, enter your GitHub username.

When it asks for your Password, paste the Personal Access Token you just generated (do not use your GitHub account password).

Method 2: Switch to SSH (Recommended for long-term use)
If you don't want to deal with tokens every time your token expires, you can switch your remote URL to use SSH (assuming you have an SSH key set up on your machine).

Run this command in your project terminal to switch the remote URL to SSH:

Bash
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:notxesnad/cret.git
Push your code again:

Bash
git push -u origin main
token expiration

To update your Personal Access Token (PAT) when it expires or if Git keeps throwing authentication errors, you need to generate a new token on GitHub and update your credentials.

Step 1: Generate a New Token on GitHub
Go to GitHub.com and log in.

Click your profile picture in the top-right corner, then click Settings.

Scroll to the very bottom of the left sidebar and click Developer settings.

Click Personal access tokens, then select Tokens (classic).

Click Generate new token -> Generate new token (classic).

Give it a descriptive note (e.g., "Vercel/CLI Token") and check the repo scope checkbox.

Scroll to the bottom and click Generate token.

Copy your new token right away.

Step 2: Update Your Git Credentials
Depending on your operating system, choose one of the options below to apply the new token:

Option A: Mac (Using Keychain Access)
Mac stores your old password in the Keychain. You can update it instantly without running terminal commands:

Press Cmd + Space, type Keychain Access, and open the app.

In the top-right search bar, type github.com.

Look for an item labeled internet password for github.com.

Double-click it, check Show password, delete your old token/password, and paste your new Personal Access Token. Click Save Changes.

Option B: Windows (Using Credential Manager)
Windows saves credentials in your control panel:

Press the Windows key, type Credential Manager, and open it.

Click on Windows Credentials.

Scroll down to look for git:[https://github.com](https://github.com).

Click on it, click Edit, replace the old password/token with your new Personal Access Token, and click Save.

Option C: Reset via Command Line (Universal)
You can force Git to prompt you for your new token on the next push by clearing the cached credentials or updating the remote URL:

Bash
git remote set-url origin https://<YOUR_NEW_TOKEN>@github.com/notxesnad/cret.git
(Replace <YOUR_NEW_TOKEN> with the token string you just copied, then run git push -u origin main)

what should i set the expiration to

When generating a Personal Access Token (PAT) on GitHub, you are asked to choose an expiration timeframe.

Set the expiration based on your preference for security vs. convenience:

30 Days or 60 Days: Best for security if this is a temporary project or if you prefer rotating credentials regularly. However, you will have to repeat the steps to generate and update your token once it expires.

90 Days: A good middle-ground default used by many developers.

No Expiration (Custom): Convenient if you never want the token to expire and want to avoid future authentication errors on your personal repository. Note: GitHub strongly discourages "No expiration" for high-security repositories, but for a simple personal real estate tool project, it saves you from having to update it again.

what should i select for scopes

When generating a Personal Access Token (PAT) for GitHub, select the following scope:

repo: Check this main box. It will automatically check all the sub-permissions underneath it (like repo:status, repo_deployment, public_repo, and delete_repo). This is required so Git has full permission to read and push code changes to your repository.

git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).

fatal: Could not read from remote repository.



Please make sure you have the correct access rights

and the repository exists.

This error (Permission denied (publickey)) means your terminal is trying to connect to GitHub using an SSH key, but your computer doesn't have an SSH key configured or linked to your GitHub account yet.

You have two ways to fix this: Option A (Switch back to HTTPS and use your Personal Access Token), or Option B (Set up an SSH key). Option A is much faster since you just generated a token.

Option A: Switch back to HTTPS (Fastest)
Run this command in your project terminal to switch your repository URL from SSH back to HTTPS:

Bash
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/notxesnad/cret.git
Then, push your code again:

Bash
git push -u origin main
When prompted for your password, paste your Personal Access Token.

Option B: Set up SSH Keys (If you prefer using SSH)
If you want to use SSH so you never have to type a password or token again, you need to generate an SSH key and add it to GitHub:

Check if you already have an SSH key:
Run this in your terminal:

Bash
ls -al ~/.ssh
If you see files like id_ed25519.pub or id_rsa.pub, skip to Step 3. Otherwise, generate a new one.

Generate a new SSH key:
Run this command (replace with your email):

Bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Press Enter to accept all default file locations and prompts (you can leave the passphrase blank).

Copy your public key:

Mac: pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

Windows (Git Bash): cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (then manually highlight and copy it)

Add the key to GitHub:

Go to GitHub.com -> Click your profile picture -> Settings.

Click SSH and GPG keys on the left sidebar.

Click New SSH key.

Give it a title (e.g., "My Laptop"), paste your key into the "Key" box, and click Add SSH key.

Test and push:
Once added, run your push command again:

Bash
git push -u origin main
great, now how do I hook my domain name up

To hook your custom domain name up to your newly deployed Next.js project on Vercel, follow these steps:

Step 1: Add the Domain in Vercel
Go to Vercel.com and open your project dashboard.

Click on the Settings tab at the top of your project page.

Select Domains from the left-hand navigation menu.

Type your domain name (e.g., coolrealestatetools.com) into the input field and click Add.

Vercel will ask you if you want to redirect the www. version to your root domain (or vice versa). Choose your preferred option and click Save.

Step 2: Configure Your DNS Records at Your Domain Registrar
Once you add the domain, Vercel will display a list of DNS records that you need to copy and paste into wherever you bought your domain (such as GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, Squarespace/Google Domains, etc.).

Typically, Vercel will ask you to add:

An A Record: Points your root domain (e.g., @ or blank) to Vercel's IP address (usually 76.76.21.21).

A CNAME Record: Points the www subdomain to cname.vercel-dns.com.

Log into the account where you purchased your domain.

Find the DNS Manager, DNS Settings, or Manage Zone section for your domain.

Add the exact records provided by Vercel and save your changes.

Step 3: Verify and Wait for SSL
Return to your Vercel Domains dashboard.

DNS changes usually take anywhere from a few minutes up to a couple of hours to propagate globally.

Once Vercel detects the correct DNS settings, it will automatically issue a free SSL certificate (https://), and your site will be live and secure on your custom domain!

Let's talk about the application login: 1) I want it to be a password-less login for users, both agents and clients.

Setting up a password-less login flow for both agents and clients is a great modern choice—it completely eliminates password fatigue, reduces support tickets for resets, and is generally much more secure.

For a real estate platform where users want quick access to tools or client portals, the industry standard is Magic Links or OTP (One-Time Passcodes) via SMS/Email.

Here is how you can implement this cleanly in your Next.js project:

1. Choose Your Authentication Strategy
Option A: Magic Links (Email) — The user types their email, receives a secure link, and clicking it logs them in instantly. (Great for agents accessing their dashboard or clients reviewing net sheets).

Option B: SMS OTP (Phone Number) — The user types their mobile number, receives a 6-digit text code, and types it in. (Extremely fast for open-house sign-ins or quick mobile access).

2. The Easiest Way to Build This in Next.js
Instead of writing a database schema, token-generation hashing, and email/SMS delivery infrastructure from scratch, you can use managed authentication providers that have built-in password-less support:

Supabase Auth: Excellent open-source backend-as-a-service. It has built-in support for Magic Links and Phone OTP out of the box with simple Next.js helper libraries (@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs).

Auth.js (formerly NextAuth.js): Highly customizable and runs directly inside your Next.js application. It supports Email providers (Magic Links) natively.

Clerk: Incredibly fast to set up for Next.js, supporting password-less SMS, email magic links, and passkeys (biometrics/FaceID) seamlessly.

3. Basic User Flow Implementation (Magic Link Example)
If you use a service like Supabase or Auth.js, the code flow in your Next.js app typically looks like this:

The Login Form Component (app/login/page.tsx):

TypeScript
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'

export default function LoginPage() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false)

  const handleLogin = async (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    // Call your auth provider here (e.g., Supabase magic link)
    // await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email })
    setSubmitted(true)
  }

  return (
    <div className="max-w-md mx-auto mt-20 p-6 bg-slate-900 rounded-3xl text-white">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-black mb-2">Sign In</h1>
      {!submitted ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleLogin} className="space-y-4">
          <input 
            type="email" 
            placeholder="Enter your email" 
            value={email}
            onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
            className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white"
            required 
          />
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 text-slate-950 font-bold py-3 rounded-xl">
            Send Magic Link
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <p className="text-emerald-400 text-center py-4">Check your email for your secure login link!</p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
Role-Based Routing After Login:
Once the user clicks their magic link or enters their OTP, your app can check their user metadata (whether they are tagged as an Agent or a Client) and route them accordingly:

Agents go to the main tool dashboard (the micro-app suite).

Clients go to a restricted view (like a specific property proposal, net sheet, or tour itinerary sent by the agent).

what do you recommend as the easiest, most light-weight and most cost effective of the 3 choices. I want both sms and email

For a Next.js project requiring both SMS and Email password-less login, the clear winner for the easiest, most lightweight, and most cost-effective solution is Supabase Auth.

Why Supabase Auth Fits Best:
Generous Free Tier: It includes up to 50,000 monthly active users (MAUs) for free, which is more than enough to launch and scale your tool suite without immediate subscription costs.

Built-in Multi-Channel Support: It natively supports both Magic Links (Email) and OTP codes (SMS) out of the box using straightforward client libraries, saving you from stitching together multiple disparate packages.

Lightweight Infrastructure: Instead of managing separate database tables for tracking verification tokens, Supabase handles user sessions, secure tokens, and user metadata seamlessly within its Postgres backend.

(Note: While Auth.js/NextAuth is also free, it does not natively manage SMS text-message routing out of the box, requiring you to manually build and hook up a third-party SMS gateway like Twilio plus custom database tracking).

let's set it up

Let’s configure Supabase password-less authentication for both Email (Magic Links) and SMS (One-Time Passcodes) in your Next.js project.

Step 1: Create Your Supabase Project
Go to Supabase.com and create a free account.

Create a New Project.

Once your database provisions, go to Project Settings > API to grab your:

Project URL (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL)

Anon / Public API Key (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)

Step 2: Install Supabase in Your Next.js Project
Open your project terminal and install the official Supabase JavaScript client:

Bash
npm install @supabase/supabase-js
Create a .env.local file in the root directory of your project to store your keys safely:

Code snippet
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=your_supabase_project_url
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_supabase_anon_key
Step 3: Configure Auth Providers in the Supabase Dashboard
Inside your Supabase Dashboard, navigate to the Authentication tab on the left.

Go to Providers:

Email: Ensure Email provider is enabled. (Supabase enables Magic Links/OTP by default).

Phone: Toggle Phone provider to Enabled.

Scroll down in the Phone provider settings and link an SMS gateway provider (such as Twilio or MessageBird) by adding your account credentials so it can send actual text messages.

Step 4: Create the Supabase Client Helper
Create a file at utils/supabase.js (or lib/supabase.js) to initialize your client:

JavaScript
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'

const supabaseUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
const supabaseAnonKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY

export const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey)
Step 5: Build a Unified Password-Less Login Component
You can create a clean toggle interface allowing users to sign in via Email or Phone (SMS) using signInWithOtp.

Create app/login/page.jsx:

JavaScript
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function LoginPage() {
  const [method, setMethod] = useState('email') // 'email' or 'phone'
  const [identifier, setIdentifier] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request') // 'request' or 'verify'
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  // 1. Request the Magic Link or SMS OTP code
  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')

    const payload = method === 'email' ? { email: identifier } : { phone: identifier }
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp(payload)

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage(method === 'email' ? 'Check your email for the link/code!' : 'Check your phone for the 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  // 2. Verify the OTP code (or confirm email token)
  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')

    const payload = method === 'email' 
      ? { email: identifier, token, type: 'email' } 
      : { phone: identifier, token, type: 'sms' }

    const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp(payload)

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.href = '/' // Redirect to your app dashboard upon success
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="max-w-md mx-auto mt-20 p-8 bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl text-white shadow-2xl">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-black mb-2">Sign In</h1>
      <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mb-6">No passwords. Fast and secure access.</p>

      {/* Switch between Email and Phone */}
      {step === 'request' && (
        <div className="flex bg-slate-800 p-1 rounded-xl mb-6">
          <button 
            type="button"
            onClick={() => { setMethod('email'); setIdentifier(''); }}
            className={`flex-1 py-2 text-xs font-bold rounded-lg transition ${method === 'email' ? 'bg-emerald-500 text-slate-950' : 'text-slate-400'}`}
          >
            Email
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button"
            onClick={() => { setMethod('phone'); setIdentifier(''); }}
            className={`flex-1 py-2 text-xs font-bold rounded-lg transition ${method === 'phone' ? 'bg-emerald-500 text-slate-950' : 'text-slate-400'}`}
          >
            Phone (SMS)
          </button>
        </div>
      )}

      {step === 'request' ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">
              {method === 'email' ? 'Email Address' : 'Phone Number (e.g. +13055551212)'}
            </label>
            <input 
              type={method === 'email' ? 'email' : 'tel'}
              placeholder={method === 'email' ? 'name@example.com' : '+13055551212'}
              value={identifier}
              onChange={(e) => setIdentifier(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition">
            Send Secure Code / Link
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter Verification Code</label>
            <input 
              type="text"
              placeholder="123456"
              value={token}
              onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-bold tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition">
            Verify & Sign In
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => setStep('request')}
            className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline mt-2"
          >
            Back / Change input
          </button>
        </form>
      )}

      {message && <p className="text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 text-emerald-400">{message}</p>}
    </div>
  )
}

Focusing purely on email magic links/OTP code authentication keeps things clean and requires zero external SMS gateway fees.

Here is how you can streamline your Supabase setup and login component to use Email Only:

1. Supabase Dashboard Check
Go to your Supabase Dashboard -> Authentication -> Providers -> Email.

Make sure it's enabled. (Supabase sends a 6-digit OTP code by default for email sign-ins when configured, or a magic link depending on your template settings).

2. The Updated Email-Only Login Component (app/login/page.jsx)
JavaScript
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function LoginPage() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request') // 'request' or 'verify'
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  // 1. Send the OTP / Magic Link to Email
  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')

    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: {
        shouldCreateUser: true, // Automatically registers new clients/agents on first login
      }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure login code!')
    }
  }

  // 2. Verify the 6-digit code entered by the user
  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')

    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.href = '/' // Redirect to your app home/dashboard
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="max-w-md mx-auto mt-20 p-8 bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl text-white shadow-2xl">
      <div className="text-center mb-6">
        <h1 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Sign In</h1>
        <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Enter your email for password-less access.</p>
      </div>

      {step === 'request' ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
            <input 
              type="email"
              placeholder="name@example.com"
              value={email}
              onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Send Login Code →
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
            <input 
              type="text"
              placeholder="123456"
              value={token}
              onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Verify & Sign In
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => setStep('request')}
            className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
          >
            Use a different email
          </button>
        </form>
      )}

      {message && (
        <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
          {message}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
actually, let's do both

Adding back SMS (Phone OTP) alongside Email gives your users maximum flexibility.

To configure SMS in Supabase, you need an SMS provider like Twilio, Vonage, or MessageBird to actually deliver the text messages to mobile phones.

Here is how to set it up step-by-step:

Step 1: Connect an SMS Provider in Supabase
Supabase uses third-party text messaging gateways to send verification codes. Twilio is the most popular and easiest choice.

Create a Twilio Account and buy a phone number that supports SMS.

Get your Account SID, Auth Token, and Twilio Phone Number from your Twilio dashboard.

Go to your Supabase Dashboard -> Authentication -> Providers -> Phone.

Enable the Phone provider.

Select Twilio as your SMS provider, paste your Twilio credentials, and click Save.

              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Verify & Sign In
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
            className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
          >
            Back / Change input method
          </button>
        </form>
      )}

      {message && (
        <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
          {message}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
actually, for now let's just do email

Keeping it strictly to email is a smart and frictionless move—it avoids external SMS gateway setup fees and complex carrier routing issues while giving users secure access.

Here is your streamlined, email-only login component ready for your app/login/page.jsx file:

JavaScript
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function LoginPage() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request') // 'request' or 'verify'
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  // 1. Send the 6-digit OTP code to the user's email
  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')

    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: {
        shouldCreateUser: true, // Automatically registers new users on their first login
      }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  // 2. Verify the code entered by the user
  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')

    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.href = '/' // Redirect to your main app dashboard
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="max-w-md mx-auto mt-20 p-8 bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl text-white shadow-2xl">
      <div className="text-center mb-6">
        <h1 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Sign In</h1>
        <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Password-less access via Email.</p>
      </div>

      {step === 'request' ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
            <input 
              type="email"
              placeholder="name@example.com"
              value={email}
              onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Send Login Code →
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
            <input 
              type="text"
              placeholder="123456"
              value={token}
              onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Verify & Sign In
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
            className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
          >
            Use a different email
          </button>
        </form>
      )}

      {message && (
        <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
          {message}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
now what

Now that you have your email-only login component built (app/login/page.jsx) and your Supabase keys set up, it’s time to test the flow and protect your main tools dashboard.

Here are the next steps to complete your authentication setup:

1. Test Your Login Flow Locally
Run your development server:

Bash
npm run dev
Open your browser to http://localhost:3000/login.

Type in your email address and click Send Login Code.

Check your email inbox for the 6-digit code sent by Supabase, type it in, and verify that it successfully redirects you back home.

2. Protect Your Main App Route (Middleware)
You want to make sure visitors can't access your micro-apps or dashboard without signing in first. Supabase provides an easy Next.js Middleware template to secure your routes.

Create a file at middleware.js in the root of your project:

JavaScript
import { createServerClient } from '@supabase/ssr'
import { NextResponse } from 'server/next'

export async function middleware(request) {
  let response = NextResponse.next({
    request: {
      headers: request.headers,
    },
  })

  const supabase = createServerClient(
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL,
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
    {
      cookies: {
        getAll() {
          return request.cookies.getAll()
        },
        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) => request.cookies.set(name, value))
          response = NextResponse.next({
            request,
          })
          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) => response.cookies.set(name, value, options))
        },
      },
    }
  )

  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()

  // If user is not signed in and trying to access the home/dashboard, redirect to /login
  if (!user && request.nextUrl.pathname === '/') {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', request.url))
  }

  return response
}

export const config = {
  matcher: ['/', '/dashboard/:path*'],
}
(Note: If you haven't installed @supabase/ssr yet for cookie handling in middleware, you can run npm install @supabase/ssr).

Runtime Error







supabaseUrl is required.



utils/supabase.js (6:37) @ module evaluation



4 | const supabaseAnonKey = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY

5 |

> 6 | export const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey)

| ^

This error happens because Next.js is not detecting your environment variables inside utils/supabase.js. When you add new environment variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY) to a .env.local file, Next.js requires a complete server restart to read them.

Here is how to fix it in two quick steps:

1. Stop your development server
Go to your terminal where npm run dev is running and press Ctrl + C to stop it.

2. Restart your development server
Run the command again:

Bash
npm run dev
Double-Check Your .env.local File
Make sure your file is named exactly .env.local (placed in the root folder right next to package.json) and that your variable names match what utils/supabase.js is looking for:

Code snippet
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=your_actual_supabase_project_url_here
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_actual_supabase_anon_key_here
Once you restart the server after saving, Next.js will pick up the keys, and the runtime error will disappear.

i don't see .env.local

If you don't see a file named .env.local in your project's root folder, it means it hasn't been created yet.

Here is how to create it in seconds:

In the root directory of your project (right alongside package.json), create a brand new file and name it exactly .env.local (make sure there are no spaces or extra file extensions like .txt at the end).

Open that file and paste your Supabase keys inside it like this:

Code snippet
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=your_actual_supabase_project_url
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_actual_supabase_anon_key
(You can copy your exact project URL and anon/public key straight from your Supabase Dashboard under Project Settings > API).

Save the file, and then restart your development server (Ctrl + C then npm run dev) so Next.js can read them.

// Built-in Email Login Component when unauthenticated
function EmailLogin() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request')
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: { shouldCreateUser: true }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.reload()
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center p-4 bg-[#0f172a] text-[#f8fafc] font-['Inter',sans-serif]">
      <div className="max-w-md w-full p-8 bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl shadow-2xl">
        <div className="text-center mb-6">
          <div className="text-xs font-bold tracking-widest text-slate-400 uppercase mb-2">
            Cool<span className="text-emerald-400">RealEstate</span>Tools.com
          </div>
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Sign In</h1>
          <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Password-less access via Email.</p>
        </div>

        {step === 'request' ? (
          <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
            <div>
              <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
              <input 
                type="email"
                placeholder="name@example.com"
                value={email}
                onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
                required
                className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
              />
            </div>
            <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
              Send Login Code →
            </button>
          </form>
        ) : (
          <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
            <div>
              <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
              <input 
                type="text"
                placeholder="123456"
                value={token}
                onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
                required
                className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
              />
            </div>
            <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
              Verify & Sign In
            </button>
            <button 
              type="button" 
              onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
              className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
            >
              Use a different email
            </button>
          </form>
        )}

        {message && (
          <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
            {message}
          </p>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

This error happens because React is trying to execute calculateNet as a JavaScript function within the React component scope, but the function was declared globally inside the <script> tag at the bottom instead of inside the HomePage component.

Here is the fixed app/page.jsx file. I moved all the helper functions (calculateNet, switchView, showCustomModal, etc.) directly into the React component scope so they are cleanly defined and accessible:

JavaScript
'use client'
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function HomePage() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null)
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)

  // Check authentication session on load
  useEffect(() => {
    async function checkUser() {
      const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
      setUser(session?.user || null)
      setLoading(false)
    }
    checkUser()
    switchView('home')
  }, [])

  const handleLogout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut()
    window.location.reload()
  }

  // View and Modal Handlers inside React scope
  const showCustomModal = (msg) => {
    const modalMsg = document.getElementById('modal-message')
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modalMsg && modal) {
      modalMsg.innerText = msg
      modal.classList.remove('hidden')
    }
  }

  const closeCustomModal = () => {
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modal) {
      modal.classList.add('hidden')
    }
  }

  const switchView = (viewId) => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.app-view').forEach(el => {
      el.classList.remove('active')
    })
    
    const targetView = document.getElementById('view-' + viewId)
    if(targetView) {
      targetView.classList.add('active')
    }
    
    const navAction = document.getElementById('nav-action')
    if(navAction) {
      navAction.style.display = viewId === 'home' ? 'none' : 'block'
    }
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const calculateNet = () => {
    const priceInput = document.getElementById('net-price')
    const payoffInput = document.getElementById('net-payoff')
    const commInput = document.getElementById('net-comm')
    const outputEl = document.getElementById('net-output')

    if (!priceInput || !payoffInput || !commInput || !outputEl) return

    const price = parseFloat(priceInput.value) || 0
    const payoff = parseFloat(payoffInput.value) || 0
    const commRate = parseFloat(commInput.value) || 0
    const commission = price * (commRate / 100)
    const closingCosts = price * 0.015
    
    const net = price - payoff - commission - closingCosts
    outputEl.innerText = '$' + (net > 0 ? net.toLocaleString('en-US', {maximumFractionDigits: 0}) : 0)
  }

  const submitOpenHouse = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.remove('hidden')

    document.getElementById('oh-name').value = ''

    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.remove('hidden')

Your micro-apps are now branded.'); switchView('home'); }} className="w-full bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-500 to-fuchsia-500 hover:from-purple-400 hover:to-fuchsia-400 text-white font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg mt-4">

        </main>

        {/* Global Footer */}
        <footer className="max-w-xl mx-auto w-full text-center pt-8 pb-2 text-xs text-slate-500 font-medium">

        </footer>

        {/* Custom Safe Modal Box */}

          <div className="bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl p-6 max-w-sm w-full text-center space-y-4 shadow-2xl">

          </div>
        </div>

      </div>
    </>
  )
}

// Built-in Email Login Component when unauthenticated
function EmailLogin() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request')
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: { shouldCreateUser: true }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.reload()
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center p-4 bg-[#0f172a] text-[#f8fafc] font-['Inter',sans-serif]">
      <div className="max-w-md w-full p-8 bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl shadow-2xl">
        <div className="text-center mb-6">
          <div className="text-xs font-bold tracking-widest text-slate-400 uppercase mb-2">
            Cool<span className="text-emerald-400">RealEstate</span>Tools.com
          </div>
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Sign In</h1>
          <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Password-less access via Email.</p>
        </div>

        {step === 'request' ? (
          <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
            <div>
              <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
              <input 
                type="email"
                placeholder="name@example.com"
                value={email}
                onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
                required
                className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
              />
            </div>
            <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
              Send Login Code →
            </button>
          </form>
        ) : (
          <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
            <div>
              <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
              <input 
                type="text"
                placeholder="123456"
                value={token}
                onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
                required
                className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
              />
            </div>
            <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
              Verify & Sign In
            </button>
            <button 
              type="button" 
              onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
              className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
            >
              Use a different email
            </button>
          </form>
        )}

        {message && (
          <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
            {message}
          </p>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

This warning happens because Next.js components should not include external script tags (like Tailwind CDN) directly inside the JSX return structure. In a Next.js project, Tailwind CSS is already compiled natively through PostCSS/Tailwind configuration rather than via a runtime script tag.

Here is the clean, updated app/page.jsx file with the Tailwind CDN script removed and all elements intact:

'use client'
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function HomePage() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null)
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)

  // Check authentication session on load
  useEffect(() => {
    async function checkUser() {
      const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
      setUser(session?.user || null)
      setLoading(false)
    }
    checkUser()
    switchView('home')
  }, [])

  const handleLogout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut()
    window.location.reload()
  }

  // View and Modal Handlers inside React scope
  const showCustomModal = (msg) => {
    const modalMsg = document.getElementById('modal-message')
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modalMsg && modal) {
      modalMsg.innerText = msg
      modal.classList.remove('hidden')
    }
  }

  const closeCustomModal = () => {
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modal) {
      modal.classList.add('hidden')
    }
  }

  const switchView = (viewId) => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.app-view').forEach(el => {
      el.classList.remove('active')
    })
    
    const targetView = document.getElementById('view-' + viewId)
    if(targetView) {
      targetView.classList.add('active')
    }
    
    const navAction = document.getElementById('nav-action')
    if(navAction) {
      navAction.style.display = viewId === 'home' ? 'none' : 'block'
    }
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const calculateNet = () => {
    const priceInput = document.getElementById('net-price')
    const payoffInput = document.getElementById('net-payoff')
    const commInput = document.getElementById('net-comm')
    const outputEl = document.getElementById('net-output')

    if (!priceInput || !payoffInput || !commInput || !outputEl) return

    const price = parseFloat(priceInput.value) || 0
    const payoff = parseFloat(payoffInput.value) || 0
    const commRate = parseFloat(commInput.value) || 0
    const commission = price * (commRate / 100)
    const closingCosts = price * 0.015
    
    const net = price - payoff - commission - closingCosts
    outputEl.innerText = '$' + (net > 0 ? net.toLocaleString('en-US', {maximumFractionDigits: 0}) : 0)
  }

// Built-in Email Login Component when unauthenticated
function EmailLogin() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request')
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: { shouldCreateUser: true }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.reload()
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center p-4 bg-[#0f172a] text-[#f8fafc] font-['Inter',sans-serif]">
      <div className="max-w-md w-full p-8 bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl shadow-2xl">
        <div className="text-center mb-6">
          <div className="text-xs font-bold tracking-widest text-slate-400 uppercase mb-2">
            Cool<span className="text-emerald-400">RealEstate</span>Tools.com
          </div>
          <h1 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Sign In</h1>
          <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Password-less access via Email.</p>
        </div>

        {step === 'request' ? (
          <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
            <div>
              <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
              <input 
                type="email"
                placeholder="name@example.com"
                value={email}
                onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
                required
                className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
              />
            </div>
            <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
              Send Login Code →
            </button>
          </form>
        ) : (
          <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
            <div>
              <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
              <input 
                type="text"
                placeholder="123456"
                value={token}
                onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
                required
                className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
              />
            </div>
            <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
              Verify & Sign In
            </button>
            <button 
              type="button" 
              onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
              className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
            >
              Use a different email
            </button>
          </form>
        )}

        {message && (
          <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
            {message}
          </p>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function HomePage() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null)

  // Check authentication session on load (optional header display)
  useEffect(() => {
    async function checkUser() {
      const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
      setUser(session?.user || null)
    }
    checkUser()
    switchView('home')
  }, [])

  const handleLogout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut()
    window.location.reload()
  }

  // View and Modal Handlers inside React scope
  const showCustomModal = (msg) => {
    const modalMsg = document.getElementById('modal-message')
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modalMsg && modal) {
      modalMsg.innerText = msg
      modal.classList.remove('hidden')
    }
  }

  const closeCustomModal = () => {
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modal) {
      modal.classList.add('hidden')
    }
  }

  const switchView = (viewId) => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.app-view').forEach(el => {
      el.classList.remove('active')
    })
    
    const targetView = document.getElementById('view-' + viewId)
    if(targetView) {
      targetView.classList.add('active')
    }
    
    const navAction = document.getElementById('nav-action')
    if(navAction) {
      navAction.style.display = viewId === 'home' ? 'none' : 'block'
    }
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const calculateNet = () => {
    const priceInput = document.getElementById('net-price')
    const payoffInput = document.getElementById('net-payoff')
    const commInput = document.getElementById('net-comm')
    const outputEl = document.getElementById('net-output')

    if (!priceInput || !payoffInput || !commInput || !outputEl) return

    const price = parseFloat(priceInput.value) || 0
    const payoff = parseFloat(payoffInput.value) || 0
    const commRate = parseFloat(commInput.value) || 0
    const commission = price * (commRate / 100)
    const closingCosts = price * 0.015
    
    const net = price - payoff - commission - closingCosts
    outputEl.innerText = '$' + (net > 0 ? net.toLocaleString('en-US', {maximumFractionDigits: 0}) : 0)
  }

  const submitOpenHouse = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.remove('hidden')
  }

  const resetOpenHouse = () => {
    document.getElementById('oh-name').value = ''
    document.getElementById('oh-phone').value = ''
    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.remove('hidden')
  }

  return (
    <>
      <div className="min-h-screen flex flex-col justify-between p-4 md:p-8 bg-[#0f172a] text-[#f8fafc] font-['Inter',sans-serif]">
        
        {/* Custom Styles Injection */}
        <style jsx global>{`
          .font-money { font-family: 'VT323', monospace; }
          .font-openhouse { font-family: 'Righteous', cursive; }
          .font-seller { font-family: 'Playfair Display', serif; font-style: italic; }
          .font-driving { font-family: 'Bungee', cursive; }
          .font-buyer { font-family: 'Syne', sans-serif; }
          .font-sellercall { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; letter-spacing: -1px; }
          .app-view { display: none; }
          .app-view.active { display: block; animation: fadeIn 0.3s ease-out; }
          @keyframes fadeIn {
            from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); }
            to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
          }
        `}</style>

        <header className="max-w-xl mx-auto w-full flex justify-between items-center mb-6">
          <div onClick={() => switchView('home')} className="text-xs font-bold tracking-widest text-slate-400 uppercase cursor-pointer hover:text-slate-300 transition">
            Cool<span className="text-emerald-400">RealEstate</span>Tools.com
          </div>
          <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
            <div id="nav-action" style={{ display: 'none' }}>
              <button onClick={() => switchView('home')} className="text-xs font-bold bg-slate-800 hover:bg-slate-700 px-4 py-2 rounded-full border border-slate-700 transition">← Back to Menu</button>
            </div>
            {user ? (
              <button onClick={handleLogout} className="text-xs font-bold bg-rose-500/10 text-rose-400 border border-rose-500/30 hover:bg-rose-500/20 px-3 py-1.5 rounded-full transition">
                Sign Out
              </button>
            ) : (
              <a href="#login-section" className="text-xs font-bold bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-400 border border-emerald-500/30 hover:bg-emerald-500/20 px-3 py-1.5 rounded-full transition">
                Sign In
              </a>
            )}
          </div>
        </header>

        {/* Main Container */}
        <main className="max-w-xl mx-auto w-full flex-1 flex flex-col justify-center">

          {/* VIEW: HOME */}
          <div id="view-home" className="app-view active space-y-4">
            <div className="text-center mb-6">

// Reusable Email Login Widget Component
function EmailLoginWidget() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request')
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: { shouldCreateUser: true }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.reload()
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl p-8 shadow-2xl">
      <div className="text-center mb-6">
        <h2 className="text-xl font-black tracking-tight">Quick Sign In / Member Access</h2>
        <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Enter your email for password-less secure sign-in.</p>
      </div>

      {step === 'request' ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
            <input 
              type="email"
              placeholder="name@example.com"
              value={email}
              onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Send Login Code →
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
            <input 
              type="text"
              placeholder="123456"
              value={token}
              onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Verify & Sign In
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
            className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
          >
            Use a different email
          </button>
        </form>
      )}

      {message && (
        <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
          {message}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
the cool fonts we had in the original index.html file aren't showing up

To get your custom fonts (Bungee, Righteous, Playfair Display, Syne, VT323) to load properly in Next.js, they need to be injected into the document <head> in your app/layout.jsx file rather than app/page.jsx. This ensures the font stylesheets load globally across your entire app before any components render.

Here is how to fix it:

1. Update your app/layout.jsx file
Make sure your root layout includes the Google Fonts stylesheet links in its head. Replace your app/layout.jsx with this:

JavaScript
import './globals.css'

export const metadata = {
  title: 'Cool Real Estate Tools',
  description: 'All Micro-App Demos',
}

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
        <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossOrigin="anonymous" />
        <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bungee&family=Inter:wght@400;700;900&family=Playfair+Display:ital,wght@1,900&family=Righteous&family=Syne:wght@800&family=VT323&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />
      </head>
      <body>
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
2. Clean up app/page.jsx
Now that the fonts are globally available in layout.jsx, you can remove the <head> block from your app/page.jsx file so it doesn't cause duplicate head warnings.

Once you save app/layout.jsx with the font links, restart your development server (Ctrl + C then npm run dev), and all your custom fonts will render instantly across your tools!

make the Quick Sign In / Member Access display on its own - not at the bottom of the page

To make the Quick Sign In / Member Access display on its own (like a dedicated view or page rather than sitting at the bottom of the main tools dashboard), you can hook it into the same switchView system as your other micro-apps.

Here is how to update your app/page.jsx so that clicking "Sign In" in the header opens it as its own dedicated full-screen view:

Updated app/page.jsx
JavaScript
'use client'
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function HomePage() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    async function checkUser() {
      const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
      setUser(session?.user || null)
    }
    checkUser()
    switchView('home')
  }, [])

  const handleLogout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut()
    window.location.reload()
  }

  const showCustomModal = (msg) => {
    const modalMsg = document.getElementById('modal-message')
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modalMsg && modal) {
      modalMsg.innerText = msg
      modal.classList.remove('hidden')
    }
  }

  const closeCustomModal = () => {
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modal) {
      modal.classList.add('hidden')
    }
  }

  const switchView = (viewId) => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.app-view').forEach(el => {
      el.classList.remove('active')
    })
    
    const targetView = document.getElementById('view-' + viewId)
    if(targetView) {
      targetView.classList.add('active')
    }
    
    const navAction = document.getElementById('nav-action')
    if(navAction) {
      navAction.style.display = viewId === 'home' ? 'none' : 'block'
    }
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const calculateNet = () => {
    const priceInput = document.getElementById('net-price')
    const payoffInput = document.getElementById('net-payoff')
    const commInput = document.getElementById('net-comm')
    const outputEl = document.getElementById('net-output')

    if (!priceInput || !payoffInput || !commInput || !outputEl) return

    const price = parseFloat(priceInput.value) || 0
    const payoff = parseFloat(payoffInput.value) || 0
    const commRate = parseFloat(commInput.value) || 0
    const commission = price * (commRate / 100)
    const closingCosts = price * 0.015
    
    const net = price - payoff - commission - closingCosts
    outputEl.innerText = '$' + (net > 0 ? net.toLocaleString('en-US', {maximumFractionDigits: 0}) : 0)
  }

  const submitOpenHouse = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.remove('hidden')
  }

  const resetOpenHouse = () => {
    document.getElementById('oh-name').value = ''
    document.getElementById('oh-phone').value = ''
    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.remove('hidden')
  }

          .font-seller { font-family: 'Playfair Display', serif; font-style: italic; }
          .font-driving { font-family: 'Bungee', cursive; }
          .font-buyer { font-family: 'Syne', sans-serif; }
          .font-sellercall { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; letter-spacing: -1px; }
          .app-view { display: none; }
          .app-view.active { display: block; animation: fadeIn 0.3s ease-out; }
          @keyframes fadeIn {
            from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); }
            to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
          }
        `}</style>

        <header className="max-w-xl mx-auto w-full flex justify-between items-center mb-6">
          <div onClick={() => switchView('home')} className="text-xs font-bold tracking-widest text-slate-400 uppercase cursor-pointer hover:text-slate-300 transition">
            Cool<span className="text-emerald-400">RealEstate</span>Tools.com

// Reusable Email Login Widget Component
function EmailLoginWidget() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [token, setToken] = useState('')
  const [step, setStep] = useState('request')
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  const handleRequestOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: { shouldCreateUser: true }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setStep('verify')
      setMessage('Check your email for your secure 6-digit code!')
    }
  }

  const handleVerifyOtp = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({
      email,
      token,
      type: 'email'
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      window.location.reload()
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl p-8 shadow-2xl max-w-md mx-auto">
      <div className="text-center mb-6">
        <h2 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Member Sign In</h2>
        <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Enter your email for password-less secure access.</p>
      </div>

      {step === 'request' ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleRequestOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
            <input 
              type="email"
              placeholder="name@example.com"
              value={email}
              onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Send Login Code →
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <form onSubmit={handleVerifyOtp} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Enter 6-Digit Email Code</label>
            <input 
              type="text"
              placeholder="123456"
              value={token}
              onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-lg font-black tracking-widest text-center text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Verify & Sign In
          </button>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => { setStep('request'); setToken(''); setMessage(''); }}
            className="w-full text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 text-center block"
          >
            Use a different email
          </button>
        </form>
      )}

      {message && (
        <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
          {message}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
the login is asking the user to input a code, but in reality they are just clicking the link in their email

To fix this so it matches your actual Supabase email configuration (where users receive a clickable magic link rather than a 6-digit code), update the EmailLoginWidget in your app/page.jsx file to use shouldCreateUser: true and remove the code-verification step.

When a user clicks the magic link in their email, Supabase automatically handles the session token in the URL and logs them in.

Replace your EmailLoginWidget function at the bottom of app/page.jsx with this updated version:

// Reusable Email Magic Link Login Widget
function EmailLoginWidget() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('')
  const [sent, setSent] = useState(false)
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  const handleSendMagicLink = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setMessage('')
    
    const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ 
      email,
      options: { 
        shouldCreateUser: true,
        emailRedirectTo: window.location.origin
      }
    })

    if (error) {
      setMessage(error.message)
    } else {
      setSent(true)
      setMessage('Check your email and click the secure link to sign in!')
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="bg-slate-900 border border-slate-800 rounded-3xl p-8 shadow-2xl max-w-md mx-auto">
      <div className="text-center mb-6">
        <h2 className="text-2xl font-black tracking-tight">Member Sign In</h2>
        <p className="text-xs text-slate-400 mt-1">Enter your email for password-less magic link access.</p>
      </div>

      {!sent ? (
        <form onSubmit={handleSendMagicLink} className="space-y-4">
          <div>
            <label className="text-xs font-bold text-slate-400 uppercase block mb-1">Email Address</label>
            <input 
              type="email"
              placeholder="name@example.com"
              value={email}
              onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
              required
              className="w-full bg-slate-800 border border-slate-700 rounded-xl px-4 py-3 text-white focus:outline-none focus:border-emerald-500"
            />
          </div>
          <button type="submit" className="w-full bg-emerald-500 hover:bg-emerald-400 text-slate-950 font-black py-4 rounded-xl transition shadow-lg">
            Send Magic Link →
          </button>
        </form>
      ) : (
        <div className="text-center space-y-4 py-4">
          <div className="text-3xl">✨</div>
          <p className="text-sm font-bold text-white">Magic link sent!</p>
          <p className="text-xs text-slate-400">Check your email inbox and click the link to log straight in.</p>
          <button 
            type="button" 
            onClick={() => { setSent(false); setEmail(''); setMessage(''); }}
            className="text-xs text-slate-400 hover:text-white underline pt-2 block mx-auto"
          >
            Use a different email
          </button>
        </div>
      )}

      {message && (
        <p className={`text-xs text-center font-medium mt-4 ${message.includes('Check') || message.includes('sent') ? 'text-emerald-400' : 'text-rose-400'}`}>
          {message}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

'use client'
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'
import { supabase } from '@/utils/supabase'

export default function HomePage() {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    async function checkUser() {
      const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
      setUser(session?.user || null)
    }
    checkUser()
    switchView('home')
  }, [])

  const handleLogout = async () => {
    await supabase.auth.signOut()
    window.location.reload()
  }

  const showCustomModal = (msg) => {
    const modalMsg = document.getElementById('modal-message')
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modalMsg && modal) {
      modalMsg.innerText = msg
      modal.classList.remove('hidden')
    }
  }

  const closeCustomModal = () => {
    const modal = document.getElementById('custom-modal')
    if (modal) {
      modal.classList.add('hidden')
    }
  }

  const switchView = (viewId) => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.app-view').forEach(el => {
      el.classList.remove('active')
    })
    
    const targetView = document.getElementById('view-' + viewId)
    if(targetView) {
      targetView.classList.add('active')
    }
    
    const navAction = document.getElementById('nav-action')
    if(navAction) {
      navAction.style.display = viewId === 'home' ? 'none' : 'block'
    }
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })
  }

  const calculateNet = () => {
    const priceInput = document.getElementById('net-price')
    const payoffInput = document.getElementById('net-payoff')
    const commInput = document.getElementById('net-comm')
    const outputEl = document.getElementById('net-output')

    if (!priceInput || !payoffInput || !commInput || !outputEl) return

    const price = parseFloat(priceInput.value) || 0
    const payoff = parseFloat(payoffInput.value) || 0
    const commRate = parseFloat(commInput.value) || 0
    const commission = price * (commRate / 100)
    const closingCosts = price * 0.015
    
    const net = price - payoff - commission - closingCosts
    outputEl.innerText = '$' + (net > 0 ? net.toLocaleString('en-US', {maximumFractionDigits: 0}) : 0)
  }

  const submitOpenHouse = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.remove('hidden')

    document.getElementById('oh-name').value = ''

    document.getElementById('oh-success').classList.add('hidden')
    document.getElementById('oh-form-container').classList.remove('hidden')
  }
